account:
Today I have followed my appointments: the morning mill inspection was unsuccessful because I did not find the miller, I returned home for lunch, handled council letters with the secretary, and attended tea with the neighbour. No correspondence has arrived. I am now inside the great hall just before the scheduled eighteen-hundred lighting inspection with the builder.

The unusual thread is repeated talk about bridge or port changes affecting bakery deliveries. I heard townsfolk repeat versions of this claim, but none supplied firsthand evidence. The baker also asked about it and explicitly called the reports vague rumours. The secretary has received no confirmed access changes or grain shortage reports. The baker told me freight delivered wheat last night and that the bread stall was well stocked. The secretary later said the baker still needed to check tomorrow's wheat reserves and would report any actual disruption. Neither the baker, the neighbour, nor I located the miller today; that leaves the grain inspection unresolved, not proof of a shortage.

The builder has reported eight installed hall lanterns and four spares, with no request for additional inspection funds. We intend to assess visibility along tables and entrances. I can see several lanterns installed in the hall, and the builder has joined me carrying one. This appears to be the planned lighting review, rather than evidence of an emergency.

The innkeeper and freight are also in the hall near its eastern table; freight is holding wheat. I do not yet know why they are here. I asked about business and firsthand delivery news, but the recorded listeners did not include freight, so I should not assume freight heard me. Their presence and the wheat could relate to ordinary trade, but I have no evidence for a particular purpose or any coordinated scheme. My priority is to complete the lighting inspection and distinguish verified supply information from circulating rumours.
